title: Gavin Harrison - Wikipedia
notes: Gavin Richard Harrison, born 28 May 1963, Harrow, England. Porcupine Tree 2002-2010 and from 2021, King Crimson 2008 and from 2013, The Pineapple Thief from 2016; earlier Renaissance, sessions with Iggy Pop, Lisa Stansfield, Paul Young. Solo Sanity & Gravity (1997), Cheating the Polygraph (2015); 05Ric. Influences Steve Gadd and Jeff Porcaro. Bruford: 'the ability to move at will through several parallel meters, whose relationship to the basic pulse can then be said to be "displaced" or "modulated"'. Read as a summary.

title: Gavin Harrison (Modern Drummer, May 2004)
notes: Joined Porcupine Tree in early 2002 for In Absentia; his books explore 'the cerebral aspects of metric modulation and beat displacement concepts'; session credits. Read as a summary.

title: Gavin Harrison (Modern Drummer, December 2006)
notes: 'I'd write out a part starting in different positions in the bar and come up with five different grooves...they were the same groove but perceived differently.' His father, a jazz trumpeter: 'I could see the beauty in minimalist expression.' Influences Gadd, Porcaro, Steve Schaeffer, Harvey Mason, John Guerin. Read as a summary with quotes.

title: The Rhythmic Illusionist (Modern Drummer, 20 November 2008)
notes: Calls Drop 'polyrhythmic madness' (press; not a device). Read as a summary.

title: Schlagzeug-Workshop: Odd Meter Grooves (bonedo.de)
notes: The Sound of Muzak: kick and snare in cells of seven sixteenths grouped 3+2+2, under hi-hat eighths stressing the quarter; Harrison calls making an odd meter feel even 'overriding'. Read as a summary.

title: The Sound Of Muzak groove (Drumeo Beat)
notes: The groove was 'originally programmed on a drum machine' by Steven Wilson; Harrison made 'hi hat changes and some ghost note additions'. Read as a summary.

title: Grooving in 3's, 4's and 5's (Gavin Harrison, Drumeo)
notes: His lesson: hi-hat foot in quarters, the kick on every third sixteenth, the ride in fives over the bar, a snare backbeat. A lesson, not a record. Read as a summary.

title: Mastery and Mystery: foreword to Rhythmic Composition (Neil Peart, Hudson Music, 2014; transcript at 2112.net)
notes: Recalls Harrison's method, 'displace that rhythm by a sixteenth note'; says the Trains drumming 'gracefully smoothes over what could be a jagged combination of rhythms'; 'if I could play like that, that is how I would play'. Read as a summary with quotes.

title: Rhythmic Composition (Gavin Harrison and Terry Branam, Hudson Music, March 2014)
notes: Branam's transcriptions of twenty Porcupine Tree parts with Harrison's commentary (Blackest Eyes, Trains, The Sound of Muzak, Futile, Halo, Anesthetize, Nil Recurring among them). The listing only; the book was not read.

title: Gavin Harrison interview (Batteria & Percussioni, Roberto Baruffaldi, January/February 2010; on Hudson Music)
notes: King Crimson's two drummers 'thraking': 'one drummer plays (bass drum and muted crash cymbal together) in patterns of 7 whilst the other drummer does the same thing but in patterns of 11'. A 12x5.5 Sonor snare, 'the snare wires are on really tight'; tuned 'for microphones'; the bass drum 'very dead'; single strokes round the toms; no splashes. Read as a summary with verbatim quotes.

title: The Rhythmic Redesign of Porcupine Tree: an interview with Gavin Harrison (PopMatters, Brice Ezell, 8 June 2015)
notes: On Cheating the Polygraph: 'metric modulation, and clever harmonies' to 'seamlessly go from one tempo into another' between paired songs; no ratio or bar. 'The rhythmic design that Meshuggah does is so beautiful.' Read as a summary with quotes.

title: The guitarguitar Interview: Gavin Harrison (8 February 2019)
notes: The Start of Something Beautiful began as 'a rhythm in 9/8 ... that then progressed to a more energetic 5/8 for the chorus'; wants complex rhythm to 'sound musical and accessible to the listener - and not just "clever"'; the music he grew up on. Read as a summary with quotes.

title: Rhythmic Illusions and Rhythmic Perspectives (Gavin Harrison; catalogue contents, Médiathèque / PointCulture)
notes: Rhythmic Illusions: Displacement (types 1 and 2), Modulation (types 1-3), Subdivision, formula and grouping, Rhythmic scales and polyrhythmic groupings, Related tempo. Rhythmic Perspectives: ostinato, polyrhythmic theory, start displacements, modulating inside formulas. Contents only, from a search summary.

title: Interview: Gavin Harrison – Immer wieder neugierig (bonedo.de, Ingo Baron, 18 April 2024)
notes: 2024 kit: Sonor SQ2, toms 8x7, 10x8, 12x9, floor toms 15x13, 16x15, bass drum 22x15, a 14x5.25 Protean signature snare; Zildjian 14in K hats, 20in K ride, 20in and 19in K Custom Dark crashes, 18in Z China, 12in Oriental China Trash, 22in Swish Knocker, 9in crash bell; snare tuning changed per song. Read as a summary.

title: Gavin Harrison versteigert sein Porcupine Tree Schlagzeug (bonedo.de, 14 February 2020)
notes: The Sonor Designer kit, Earth finish, his Porcupine Tree tour and recording kit 2003-2007, Fear of a Blank Planet among it. Read as a summary.
